name: trim
about: Trim windows (A/B), fade-in at A, fade or cut at B: what set_trim stores, what _start sets on the deck, and the gain curve near B.

scenario.input: the `stored` trim dict is written straight into playlists[0]['trims'] (an old file), then trim_range is read

trim_range_of_stored_data._info: file is 10 s; trim_range clamps stored values: A at most 0.5 s before the end; a window under 0.5 s falls back to the end of the file

scenario.input: set_trim(playlist 0, track 0, row.set) from an empty trim for each row

windows._info: file is 10 s. range_s = (A, B) in file seconds; set_trim REFUSES a window shorter than 0.5 s (accepted false, nothing stored); A is held 0.5 s before the end; fade_out_ms = own fade_ms else config trim_fade_ms (1500); the fade-in is applied only while start == 'fade'

scenario.input: set_trim(row.trim), then _start(playlist 0, track 0, offset = row.offset seconds into the file); the deck is read right away

deck_start._info: what _start sets on the Deck. base = where in the file the sound begins, duration = length of one pass of the window

rows.case: A and B, fade at B
A and B, cut at B

fade_out_ahead_of_B._info_live_after: live_after true = nothing is live at ended_check_at_s (6.25 s)
fade_out_ahead_of_B._info: window 0..6 s, fade_ms 2000: the fade (cos) starts when 2 s are left and ends at B; then the track ends by itself

fade_in_at_A._info: fade_in_ms 1500: sin(x*pi/2) up to full level

scenario.input: each `stored` trim dict is written straight into playlists[0]['trims'] (old data; set_trim would refuse some of them), then trim_range, dur_eff and _start (from the start) are read

short_window_stored._info: file is 10 s. trim_range: A is first held to at most file - 0.5 s; then, when B < A + 0.5 (B missing counts as the end), B BECOMES THE END OF THE FILE and A is KEPT (so [2.0, 10.0], not the whole file). Exactly 0.5 s is long enough. A fallen-back window has no out-fade (hi = end of file)
short_window_stored._info_tolerance_by_key: positions and durations in file seconds are compared within one sample (2.5e-5 s): Deck.duration is sound.get_length() of the cut Sound, whose frame range is [int(lo * 48000), int(hi * 48000)), so In 2.0 / Out 2.51 gives 24479 samples = 0.509979 s (int(2.51 * 48000) = 120479 in floating point), while hi_s, range_s and dur_eff_s are the exact float seconds (2.51, 0.51); a whole-frame engine gets 0.51 for the duration

scenario.input: set_trim(playlist 0, track 0, row.set) from an empty trim for each row

set_trim_rounding_a_b._info: values are rounded to 0.01 s (round(v, 2)). An In that is <= 0.01 s after rounding is not stored (so 0.01 is dropped and 0.02 is the smallest stored In); an Out that is >= file length - 0.01 s after rounding is not stored; an Out past the end is first clipped to the file length (and then dropped)

scenario.input: set_trim(row.set) from an empty trim (the row with `previous` starts from {in 1.0, out 5.0})

set_trim_minimum_window._info: the window is checked AFTER rounding and only when both A and B are stored: B < A + 0.5 is refused (accepted false, nothing changes), exactly 0.5 s is accepted. B alone (no A) is accepted whatever it is, but a stored B under 0.5 s then falls back to the end of the file when played (see short_window_stored); range_s shows that

scenario.input: set_trim(playlist 0, track 2, row.set) from an empty trim; the file is 10.004 s

set_trim_out_vs_file_length._info: the Out is compared with the file length itself, not with a rounded length: Out >= 10.004 - 0.01 (= 9.994) is dropped, so 9.99 is stored here but was dropped for a file of exactly 10 s; an Out past the end is clipped to the length rounded to 0.01 s (10.0)

scenario.input: set_trim(playlist 0, track 1, {out 20, fade_ms or fade_in_ms = value}) from an empty trim; the window (20 s) is longer than every value

fade_length_limits._info: both lengths are rounded to whole ms and must be 100..10000 ms (inclusive): outside that set_trim refuses everything in the call (accepted false, nothing stored). 99.4 rounds to 99 (refused), 99.6 to 100 (accepted)

scenario.input: set_trim(playlist 0, track 1, row.set) from an empty trim for each row

fade_length_held_to_window._info: a fade length is held to the part that plays (B - A; the fade-in with no B: the rest of the file) but never below 100 ms; a fade length with no B is dropped (it belongs to B); the length is kept while the edge is Cut (end cut / start absent)

scenario.input: set_trim(playlist 0, track 1, row.set) one after the other WITHOUT clearing between rows (each row changes what the previous one left)

fade_length_follows_window_changes._info: a stored fade length is re-clamped whenever the window shrinks, and never grows back when the window is widened again (row 2); removing B drops the fade length (last row)

default_fade_longer_than_window._info: window [2, 3] (1 s) with the default 1500 ms fade (trim_fade_ms): the deck is started with end_fade_ms 1500, but Deck.update holds the fade to the length of one pass, so it starts at once (t = 0) and runs the whole window

out_fade_placement_loop._info: window [0, 4], fade_ms 1000. The out-fade runs only in the LAST pass of a deck that ends; a looping deck never ends and never out-fades (vol stays 1 through every lap)

out_fade_placement_once._info: window [0, 4], fade_ms 1000. The out-fade runs only in the LAST pass of a deck that ends; two passes of the 4 s window: no fade in pass 1, the out-fade only in pass 2 (7 s .. 8 s), then it ends

out_fade_placement_default._info: window [0, 4], fade_ms 1000. The out-fade runs only in the LAST pass of a deck that ends; out-fade over the last second of the window (3 s .. 4 s), then it ends

out_fade_placement_stop._info: window [0, 4], fade_ms 1000. The out-fade runs only in the LAST pass of a deck that ends; same as default: stop only decides what follows

out_fade_once_switched_off_in_pass_1._info: once switched off in pass 1: that pass becomes the last one, so the out-fade runs at its end (3 s .. 4 s) and the deck ends at 4 s

loop_switched_off_in_pass_1_end._info: loop switched off in pass 1: the running pass is played out and the deck ends at B (4 s). ONLY THE END IS CONTRACT. What the level does in that last pass is a Python quirk (AUDIO-SPEC quirk 10): the deck was started looping, so Python never out-fades it and it stops dead at B; the ideal (a port may do it) is the out-fade 3 s .. 4 s like the default case. The measured levels are in _info_python_vol.

scenario.input: set_trim(row.trim), set_end(0, 0, 'loop'), then _start(playlist 0, track 0, offset = row.offset_s [, paused / crossfade_ms]); the deck is read right away

fade_in_start_threshold._info: TWO thresholds, both on `offset` = the position handed to _start, in FILE seconds (not relative to A). (1) fade-in: applied only when offset <= 0.05 s (0.05 yes, 0.0501 no), not paused and not under a crossfade; a start at offset = A itself (2.0 here) is a part-way start and does NOT fade in. (2) deck.fresh (the loop / once / trigger gate, 'at the In point'): |start - A| < 0.06 s where start = A for offset <= 0.05 else max(A, offset); 2.05 is fresh, 2.06 is not (0.0599 / 0.06 with A = 0). base_s = where the sound begins: offsets below A start at A
fade_in_start_threshold._info_tolerance_by_key: base_s is the exact float offset handed to _start (max(A, offset): 0.0501, 0.0599 with A = 0), not a frame count; 0.0501 s is 2404.8 samples, so a whole-frame engine differs by up to 4.2e-6 s. offset_s is the input itself (same value)

scenario.input: set_trim(row.set), then _start from the start (offset 0); the deck is read right away

fade_in_cap._info: fade_in_ms of the deck = min(stored fade-in, window - out-fade) when that is >= 100 ms (inclusive: 100 left is kept, 99 left is not); otherwise it is min(stored fade-in, window) and the out-fade is NOT shortened (they then overlap: see fade_in_out_fade_overlap). end_fade_ms is 0 for a Cut at B or no B; the default out-fade (trim_fade_ms 1500) counts even when longer than the window

rows.case: 1 s window, out-fade 900, fade-in 500 (100 ms left)
1 s window, out-fade 901, fade-in 500 (99 ms left)
Out is Cut (no out-fade), 0.5 s window, fade-in 500

fade_in_out_fade_overlap_901._info: Only the deck values are contract (the fade-in keeps its whole length, the out-fade is not shortened). What the level does while they overlap is Python's (AUDIO-SPEC quirk 11, in _info_python_vol, not compared): the out-fade cannot start while another fade is running, so it starts at the first tick after the fade-in ends and runs over what is left (901: from 0.5 s, 0.5 s long; 1000: never, the deck ends at full level at B). A port may multiply the two envelopes instead.

fade_in_out_fade_overlap_1000._info: Only the deck values are contract (the fade-in keeps its whole length, the out-fade is not shortened). What the level does while they overlap is Python's (AUDIO-SPEC quirk 11, in _info_python_vol, not compared): the out-fade cannot start while another fade is running, so it starts at the first tick after the fade-in ends and runs over what is left (901: from 0.5 s, 0.5 s long; 1000: never, the deck ends at full level at B). A port may multiply the two envelopes instead.
